ai.title: Stop applying gray color to newlines in tool renderers
ai.summary: Refactored tool renderers in npm-app/src/utils/tool-renderers.ts to stop wrapping newline characters with the gray color function. Changed multiple return statements from gray('\n') to plain '\n' or separated the color call from the newline. This prevents the ANSI escape codes for color from being applied to invisible whitespace characters, potentially avoiding rendering artifacts in the terminal.

eli5.text: When you run a tool in the terminal, the tool's output now uses color only around visible text, not around the blank line breaks between lines of text. Previously, those line breaks were wrapped in color codes too, which sometimes caused garbled display in the terminal. You will notice slightly cleaner output formatting, especially around tool results and progress indicators.

ai.title: Root typecheck orchestrates build and typecheck-only across workspace
ai.summary: Root package.json typecheck now runs build then typecheck-only across common, packages, backend, npm-app, and web. Workspace packages gained typecheck-only and build-and-typecheck scripts, plus explicit common and code-map workspace dependencies. web renamed from codebuff-web to web. This ensures tsc-alias and contentlayer steps execute in the correct order during typechecking.

eli5.text: The app's self-check process now runs the full build first across all parts of the project, then checks each piece for mistakes. This means the web frontend (recently renamed from codebuff-web to web) and shared code libraries now build and check themselves in the correct order, so steps like converting modern code paths and loading content layers happen at the right time. If you ran the app's internal quality check today, it would now catch more build-time errors before they become problems.

ai.title: backend build script uses tsc --build
ai.summary: backend/package.json build script switched from tsc to tsc --build. Enables incremental compilation and project references. No user-facing behavior change.

eli5.text: The system that turns the assistant's source code into a working program now builds only the parts that have changed instead of recompiling everything from scratch each time. This means future background setup runs on the developer side finish faster, but you won't notice anything different when using the assistant. The change is purely internal and has no effect on your experience today.

ai.title: Fix multiline command echo skipping in terminal.ts
ai.summary: Refactors runCommandPty in npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts to dynamically calculate linesToSkip based on command length instead of a static foundFirstNewLine flag. This ensures all lines of a multiline command are correctly skipped from the output stream before processing begins. Scope limited to internal terminal utility logic.

eli5.text: When you run a command that spans multiple lines, the assistant would sometimes skip part of what you typed instead of skipping the whole thing at once. Now it counts how many lines your command has and skips exactly that many lines from the output stream before starting to show you results, so multi-line commands no longer leave extra or missing text behind. This affects only the internal terminal handling behind the scenes, so if you looked, you'd notice cleaner output after running multi-line commands, though there's no visible new feature or setting.

ai.title: Simplify terminal command echo skip logic
ai.summary: Replaced multi-line command echo skipping with a single-line check in `runCommandPty`. The previous logic attempted to skip all lines corresponding to the command input, which caused issues with flaky terminal outputs or multi-line commands. The new logic strictly skips only the first line of output, assuming it is the command echo. This change is isolated to `npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts`.

eli5.text: When you run a command in the terminal, the tool would sometimes show or hide the wrong parts of the output, making it look flaky or confusing, especially with longer commands. The system now consistently skips just the first line it sees (which is the echoed command) instead of trying to guess how many lines to hide. You wouldn't notice a new feature, but the terminal output should look steadier and more predictable when commands run.

Updated `defaultToolCallRenderer` in `npm-app/src/utils/tool-renderers.ts` to insert double newlines before and after tool call output. `onToolStart` now prefixes with '

' and `onToolEnd` returns '

' to separate tool logs from surrounding text.

eli5.text: When the assistant searches for files, the tool's status messages now have extra blank lines above and below them, creating clear visual separation from surrounding text. If you watched the assistant search for files, you'd notice the labeled status header (like "Find Files") now sits in its own paragraph with breathing room before and after. This is a minor visual adjustment and is live today.

ai.title: Global stdout newline squashing replaces Client.displayChunk
ai.summary:
New `npm-app/src/display.ts` module intercepts `process.stdout.write` and `process.stderr.write` to globally squash consecutive newlines (`
{3,}` to `

`). This mechanism replaces the previous `Client.displayChunk` method, requiring all direct output calls in `npm-app/src/client.ts` and `npm-app/src/cli.ts` to use standard `process.stdout.write` or `console` methods. The squash feature is enabled via `enableSquashNewlines()` in `npm-app/src/index.ts` and `npm-app/src/cli.ts`, and disabled via `disableSquashNewlines()` before user input prompts. This ensures consistent spacing across all CLI output surfaces, including tool results and error logs.

eli5.text: When you run commands in the tool, any time the output has three or more blank lines in a row, the software now automatically squashes that down to just two blank lines. This happens everywhere the tool prints text - command results, error messages, status updates - so nothing has extra gaps anymore. The change took effect today for the assistant's responses to your commands.
